title: Associated flat modules are flat over their affine base
statement: Let $T$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-morphism-conventions], $A=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ and $M$ a flat $A$-module. Associate its sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec} A$ and pull it back along the canonical affine isomorphism $T\to\operatorname{Spec} A$. The resulting $\mathcal O_T$-module is flat over $\operatorname{id}_T$ in the affine-section sense of [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]: for affine opens $W\subseteq Z$ of $T$, its sections on $W$ are flat over $\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_T)$ via restriction. No complex, cover or cohomology assertion is included.

source.place: Tags 01I9 (1), 00HT; affine open immersions are flat

proof.text: The canonical affine chart identifies T with Spec A. For affine W, the affine pullback formula identifies sections of the associated module with Gamma(W,O) tensor_A M. Base change of the flat module M is flat over Gamma(W,O).

For affine W contained in affine Z the inclusion is an open immersion, hence flat. Its ring map Gamma(Z,O) to Gamma(W,O) is flat by the affine criterion for a flat morphism. Flatness transitivity proves the required section condition. Naturality of the pullback-section identification gives the scalar action specified by IsFlatOver of the identity, and the empty-open case gives a zero module.
